Gaps (10-K line items, proxy detail, TAC magnitude, early 10yr series) remain haircuts, not vetoes.

THESIS INTACT, no break in 6 weeks. Integrated hardware+software personal-computing ecosystem anchored by a 2B+ active installed base, monetized by ~70%-margin Services (annuity: hardware one-time sales convert to recurring high-margin Services). REGIME REINFORCES the 'quality compounder' read: the 7/28 semiconductor crash + rotation OUT of AI-hardware/memory/Korea INTO value/defensives drove a flight-to-quality bid into Apple (crossed $5T, reclaimed #1 from NVDA). News explicitly attributes Apple's outperformance (+~25% YTD vs NVDA +~6%) to 'a deliberate decision to stay largely on the sidelines of the costly AI infrastructure race that has pressured cash flows at many of its Big Tech peers' -- i.e., the capex-light annuity model is being repriced as the defensive winner of the capex-audit regime. Theme is stronger relatively; the question remains PRICE and AI-era entry durability.

Moat UNCHANGED and durable: ecosystem switching cost + brand pricing power + custom SoC + App Store two-sided platform; installed-base annuity HIGH (no erosion; Services +16.3% Q2). OPERATOR UPDATE (closes 6/19 O3): CEO succession is now RESOLVED, not open -- Tim Cook becomes executive chairman and John Ternus (SVP Hardware Engineering, 25-yr insider, 'product person') becomes CEO effective 2026-09-01 (announced 2026-04-20, unanimous board, orderly long-planned transition; 2026-07-30 is Cook's final earnings call). This REDUCES the 6/19 key-man/late-tenure haircut (uncertainty over WHETHER Cook leaves is resolved via the good kind of succession) but introduces a smaller NEW watch: Ternus's capital-allocation discipline is unproven, and the disciplined-buyback per-share engine (Cook 5/5) is central to the return thesis. CXMT/memory regime item is NOT a threat to Apple -- Apple is a memory BUYER, so a new DRAM entrant deflating the memory scarcity premium is a mild COGS tailwind, the opposite of the memory names. Net durability HIGH; would support Core-level size IF price allowed. Operator grade holds ~4/5.

Owner earnings unusually clean and, in THIS regime, a RELATIVE STRENGTH: capex-light (FY25 capex $12.7B / revenue $416B = 3%), FCF ~= net income (no NVDA-style equity-gain distortion), TTM NI ~$122.6B, TTM FCF ~$129B, owner-earnings anchor ~$120B (conservative). Fortress balance sheet: net cash ~$61.9B. Per-share engine ~2.5-4%/yr share shrink. In the 'AI-capex audit year' Apple is NOT the one being stress-tested on $125-200B/yr capex->FCF conversion (it rents AI compute via Google cloud / Nvidia GPUs rather than building it) -- the 6/19 'AI laggard' negative is, financially, a relative positive here. NO NEW APPLE EARNINGS in the 6/19->7/28 window: the June quarter (fiscal Q3 FY26) reports 2026-07-30 (2 days after as_of); consensus rev ~$109-110B / EPS ~$1.89 are ESTIMATES only, not owner-earnings inputs. M4 quality carried, not freshly re-confirmed -> confidence MED; the 7/30 print is the key near-term catalyst.

No structural impairment / no balance-sheet death (net cash $61.9B) -> still no hard veto. But the -1 is now dominated by ELEVATED valuation / mean-reversion risk: the +14% run to a rotation-driven 52wk high (41.7x OE, 2.4% yield) is a sentiment/flight-to-safety spike, NOT an earnings-driven re-rating (no new report), so mean-reversion risk is higher than 6/19; FOMC Wednesday with a (hawkish-leaning) Warsh press conference adds multiple-compression risk to a 41.7x long-duration 2.4%-yield asset. Crucially, the regime risks hammering peers mostly DO NOT apply to Apple: AI-capex-audit (capex-light), CXMT/memory deflation (Apple is a buyer -> tailwind). Google TAC search-remedy (O1) unchanged margin haircut; App Store global take-rate (F3) remains the only path that could escalate toward veto (needs multi-year global synchrony; not now). Transition risk: Ternus could alter capital-allocation discipline (watch, not veto). This is the INVERSE of a false-cheap trap -- it is a false-EXPENSIVE setup: overpaying for a genuine compounder at a rotation high. Price, not durability, is the binding constraint.

runner_dissent: Carried from 6/19 (the 2016 SEVERE-UNDERSIZE lesson: do not under-ceiling a genuine compounder on a maturity narrative; I keep durability HIGH and let PRICE do the capping) -- PLUS three 7/28-specific points. (1) NEW MONEY got WORSE, not better: unlike the 6 peers that fell 16-37% (improving their entry IRR), AAPL's +14% run to a rotation-driven 52wk high cut base 5y IRR from +2.7% to ~0.0% and widened the premium over buy-below to +47%. A firmer WATCH is the correct, objective response; this is not timidity (2016 was cheap at ~10x + net cash 31% of cap; today is ~41.7x + net cash 1.24%). (2) The EXISTING-POSITION call is the genuine tension this run. For the first time the TRIM case is materially live -- NOT because weight got large (invalid per methodology; Duan let Apple run to ~60%) but because valuation approaches 'absurd vs value' (trigger #2: ~41.7x OE, ~0% base IRR on a low-single-digit grower) AND the regime handed a clean rotation opportunity (trigger #3: 6 other quality Mega7 names now 16-37% cheaper). I keep the single-name verdict at HOLD (exceptional durable compounder, no impairment, ongoing buyback accretion, orderly succession -- methodology says do not sell winners for being expensive), but an honest reader should treat this as HOLD-LEANING-TRIM: a light trim-to-rotate is defensible for an overweight holder and belongs to the Portfolio-Controller/Synthesis layer, not this card. (3) Cook->Ternus succession RESOLVES 6/19 O3 (net risk-reducer: orderly 25-yr insider transition), replacing key-man uncertainty with a smaller unproven-capital-allocator watch -- not thesis-breaking. Concentration note (METHODOLOGY §5): AAPL is the ONE Mega7 whose regime tailwind is flight-FROM-AI-capex, so it DIVERSIFIES a book otherwise long 'AI capex + liquidity' -- a point FOR holding it over the hardware names, but the entry price erases that edge for NEW money. Residual OPEN kept honest: TAC magnitude (O1), AI-entry monetization (O4), 10-K line items (O2), early 10yr series (O5), and the unseen 2026-07-30 print.
